data.name: Illusion: A Tale of the Mind
data.detailed_description:
Illusion is a puzzle exploration game set in the ambience of the early 1920’s Parisian cabaret.
Step into the shoes of a young girl named Emma and live her adventures as she is trapped inside the mind of a mad man.

Embark on her journey through the mind’s-eye of her captors, living in a fractured world of old memories and festering wounds, that paradoxically reveals itself to be also a place of great beauty and intrigue.

Embrace the Illusion!

Features:


  • A sinister and touching story
  • Breath-taking mind’s-eye levels
  • Beauty and death melded via surrealist inspired art
  • Dark tale scarred by the Great War
  • Taste the horror of war and fragility of life

reviews.review:
I have mixed feelings about this game so take this positive review with a grain of salt. First of all, this point&click puzzle game is just the first episode with 3 chapters, which means the story does not have a final conclusion. Based on the poor sales of the game, I have to assume that we are not going to get the second episode. It took me about 5 hours to beat it, which is a little longer than I expected - considering its creative level design. To my surprise, there are certain aspects of this title that I really enjoyed, such as beautiful scenery, psychological themes, interesting use of cameras, and a sad story. It's not a complete disaster like Sonic 06, but you will need a lot of patience to tolerate some of its less ideal elements. 

[h1] Technical Problems: [/h1]

Let's get the elephant out of the way - the game requires you to hold the left mouse button to move, as opposed to just clicking. So technically it is not a point&click game, but rather a game that should have been a point&click. I think they implemented these controls for the chasing sequences, but holding the mouse is not exactly the best way of doing it either. In regards to those running away sequences, they can be pretty frustrating because it takes a long time to respawn, plus the checkpoints are not very friendly. However, most of the game is just solving casual puzzles, anyone can do it. Unfortunately, many of the puzzles happen off-screen, so you constantly have to move around to see what is going on. Also, the game does not have a chapter select, so if you missed some achievements, you will have to do a full circle. There are many more small things that I could mention, but those are the main problems that I would consider to be very damaging to the experience.

[h1] Puzzle Gameplay: [/h1]

80% of the puzzles have something to do with alignment - moving your camera for example. The other 20% are like jigsaw puzzles and activating switches. As I said earlier, some of the things happen outside of your view, so it can be very annoying. I will say that I enjoyed the visual aspect of those puzzles, as the stages are generally designed around the riddle. I personally did not find the game to be very cryptic or difficult. Overall it has a nice variety of puzzles if you into that kind of gameplay, even though sometimes it takes a long time to find hidden glass shards to progress.

[h1] Narrative / Visuals: [/h1]
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1547977431 (this is the main reason I did not give it a negative review, some* parts of this game are just beautiful)

This game is not consistent when it comes to visuals and narrative. You could probably nitpick the voice acting as well, but that is the least of your worries. Some stages look like they were made in 2010, while other levels have some of the best backgrounds I have ever seen in a video game. I did not enjoy the story by the end of chapter 1, chapter 2 however, was a lot better. You know, it did manage to pull on my heartstrings even though the "plot twist" was very predictable. Most of the story revolves around 4 characters, and I think the game did a decent job developing their background. I can also see some narrative similarities to [i] Contrast [/i], I wonder if it was vaguely inspired by it.

[b] Pros: [/b]

+ interesting visuals / some* stages are gorgeous
+ psychological themes 
+ surreal puzzle design
+ decent story 

[b] Cons: [/b]

- sluggish controls
- clunky chase sequences
- subpar settings
- some off-screen puzzles
- no chapter select
- poor consistency with art and story
Bonus Con (!) - you think they will make EP2?

[h1] Overall Thoughts: 6/10 [/h1]

I don't dislike the game, but it could have been so much better. Considering the lack of conclusion for the story, I completely understand if nobody wants to buy this. The devs made some poor design decisions, especially with those controls. I assume the game either lacked funding or talent because it is obviously not polished. Even after all of the bad things that I mentioned, I think it's alright. If anything, I really liked looking at some of the stages, and the narrative was somewhat compelling. 

[code]Review By: http://store.steampowered.com/curator/31294838-Hidden-Gem-Discovery/ [/code]
